# Preflight — 1.3 `pr hold`, 1.4 `deploy:` setting and `phase deployed --land`

*Source of record — do not edit.* Recon was two Explore passes (launch seam; pr/settings/deployed
seam) synthesised in-session. (1.1–1.2 ran without a preflight; noted in the handoff.)

## Findings that change the plan

1. **A failed body read must never become a body write.** `GhClient.call` (`T/pr/gh.ts:32-44`)
   ignores exit codes and `PR_FIELDS` (`:19`) has no `body`. Appending *How to review* needs the
   current body; reading it through a client that treats a failed read as empty would replace the
   PR description with the section alone. The read goes in `GhWrites` beside the writes, exit code
   checked (the interface comment at `T/pr/actions/gh-writes.ts:24` already gives that reason).
2. **`pr hold` must be idempotent.** A babysitter rerun (or a relaunch after a crash) calls it twice.
   Replace an existing `## How to review` section (up to the next `## ` heading) instead of appending
   a second one; `gh label create --force` makes the label step safe to repeat.
3. **Target shape follows the house idiom, not `<n>` alone.** Every `pr` action takes
   `[<pr> | <spec-name> [<group>]]` through `resolvePr` (`T/pr/actions/rerun.ts:24-26`,
   `T/commands/pr/rerun.ts:4`). `pr hold` does the same and refuses a PR that isn't open.
4. **Doctor's gate check hard-codes `gates.`** (`T/doctor/settings.ts:21-22,31`). `deploy.gate` needs
   the full key in the list (`{ key: "gates.per-commit" | "deploy.gate", name }`), a small refactor
   in the same commit as the `deploy:` key.
5. **`phase deployed` is sync** (`T/commands/phase.ts:16,36,58-73`); `--land` is async
   (`landOnMain`, `T/core/land-on-main.ts:23`). `PhaseAction.run` / `phaseCommand` widen to
   `string | Promise<string>` (`spec.ts:41` already accepts a Promise; existing tests call the sync
   actions and stay valid). The land path goes in its own file (`T/phases/deployed-land.ts`), reusing
   `planDeployed` on the tip's spec folder: its single `progress.md` edit fits `MainEditPlan`'s
   one-file write, and its `phase.done` check runs against main, which is right after a merge.

## Canon against the chunk

| Rule | Verdict | Consequence |
|------|---------|-------------|
| SRP | Bites | `hold.ts` orchestrates; the section splice is a pure `withHowToReview(body, section)` with its own tests |
| DIP | Bites | the action gets `Runner` through deps like `RerunDeps`; no `systemRunner` inside |
| Errors are values | Bites | every gh step returns `Result`; the first failure ends the action with `pr hold: <reason>`, nothing after it runs |
| Single source of truth | Bites | label name `hold-for-review` is one exported constant (board's `pr-review` kinds read it in phase 2) |
| Size caps | Bites | `gh-writes.ts` 97 → ~125 lines; `commands/phase.ts` 134 → ~145; both under 250 |
| Clean Architecture / DDD | Inert | CLI tool code, no domain layer |

## Amendments

1. `GhWrites` gains `body(pr)`, `setBody(pr, text)` (`gh pr edit <n> --body-file -`, stdin) and
   `label(pr, name)` (`gh label create <name> --force …` then `gh pr edit <n> --add-label <name>`).
2. `pr hold [<pr> | <spec> [<group>]] --how-to-review <file>`; the file's text gets a
   `## How to review` heading when it lacks one. Result line: `Held: #<n> · label hold-for-review · How to review in the PR`.
3. Settings: `deploy: { paths: [globs], gate: <section> }` parsed only when both are present (one
   problem line otherwise); `Settings:` part `deploy: gate <name> for <n> paths`.
4. Doctor gate list carries full keys; `deploy.gate` joins it.
5. `phase deployed <spec> <phase> --land` → `landDeployed`; result `Phase <id> marked deployed <day> on <branch>`;
   `unchanged` (already marked on main) is success; refusals pass through as `phase deployed: …`.

None.
